$comment: Reviewed exceptions to the dependency advisory audit. Every entry needs an
advisory id, a reason someone actually reasoned about, and an expiry date.
Release runs honour these regardless of expiry, so a lapsed date can never
block a deploy on a day nobody chose. The scheduled dependency-audit job
fails on a lapsed entry instead, which forces review on a real deadline
without coupling it to whoever merges next.
Adding an entry is a security decision, not a build fix. Say why the risk is
acceptable, not merely that the build is red.

exceptions.reason: rwsdk depends on decompress@4.2.1 and no patched release exists upstream. Carried over verbatim in effect from the inline `--ignore GHSA-mp2f-45pm-3cg9` that release.yml passed to `bun audit` before this file existed, so it changes no security posture: the advisory was already suppressed on the release path.
exceptions.risk_assessment: UNVERIFIED — nobody has confirmed whether decompress can be reached with attacker-controlled archives in our build. The pre-existing suppression carried no such analysis either. Until an owner of the rwsdk build path assesses reachability and replaces this field, treat the exception as inherited, not justified.

exceptions.reason: rwsdk's browser installer pins extract-zip@2.0.1 and no patched upstream release exists. The transitive package is locally patched to reject absolute and out-of-root symlink targets before creating the link; a generated malicious-archive regression test pins that behavior.
exceptions.risk_assessment: Reachability is limited to the build-time rwsdk browser downloader, not the deployed Worker or browser bundle. The local patch also closes the published traversal primitive if that build path later receives an attacker-controlled archive. Remove this exception and patch when the tracked framework upgrade removes extract-zip.
